BrokerCapabilities.description:
What a live broker is and what it serves, read from its policy alone. Never a local path,
a grant, an environment value or a credential, and no permission to run anything.

api_version.description: The wire API version the broker speaks.

exec_policy.description: `account`: anything this OS account can run. `granted`: only the operator's grants.

shell_commands.description: Whether a `command` line runs on the machine's shell (an `account` broker only).

supported_requests.description:
The request methods this broker answers under its policy; one it always refuses (a
`granted` broker's processes, settings changes and web reads) is left out. Listed is
not granted: the broker still checks each request.

workspace_scope.description:
`account`: files and jobs anywhere the account reaches. `workspace`: only inside the
broker's workspace.

ChangesInput.description:
Wait until the broker's operations change as a list shows them: one admitted, retired,
or moved to another state (output alone is not a change here). For a view that
re-lists only when something changed, instead of on a timer.

after_revision.description:
The revision your list reflects (from the last answer). Absent: answer at once with
the current revision. A broker that restarted answers at once, too.

timeout_ms.description: Longest to wait, 1..=50000 milliseconds; at the limit the same revision comes back.

value.description: The new value, a whole number.

account.description: The OS account the broker runs as, and its home directory (what `~` means).

allowed_executables.description: The programs a `granted` broker runs (canonical paths).

changed.description: What the last change did, for `set_config_value`.

config_file.description: The broker.json this broker was started from, when it was started from one.

exec_policy.description: `account`: anything this OS account can run. `granted`: only `allowed_executables`.

max_operations.description: Jobs kept, running and finished; the oldest finished one is retired past this.

operations_held.description: Jobs held now, and how many of them are running.

output_limit_bytes.description: Output kept per job, in bytes.

workspace.description: Where a relative path and a job without `cwd` start (canonical).

path.description:
Path (absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the workspace) of the directory to make; missing parents are made too. An existing
directory is not an error.

bytes_base64.description: The raw bytes, base64, when they are not text.

eof.description: Whether this page reached the end of the file.

identity.description:
Which file object was read: device and inode on Unix, volume serial and file ID on
Windows. It stays through a rename and changes when the file is replaced by another, so
pages read in turn are known to be of one file when it is the same on each.

next_line.description:
Read by lines: the `start_line` to read on from, when lines remain and the number
is known. A single line longer than `max_bytes` is read on by bytes, from
`next_offset`.

next_offset.description: The offset to read on from.

size.description: The file's size in bytes when it was read.

start_line.description:
Read by lines: the 1-based number of the first line returned, when known (always
for a positive `start_line`; from the end, for files up to 8 MiB).

text.description:
The bytes as text, when they are UTF-8 text. A character split at the end of the
page is left for the next read.

total_lines.description:
Read by lines: the file's line count, for files up to 8 MiB, or once a read from a
known line number reaches the end.

expected_replacements.description:
How many times `old_text` must occur (default 1); every occurrence is replaced, and
a different count changes nothing.

new_text.description: Text to put in its place.

old_text.description: Exact text to find, including whitespace and line endings.

path.description: Path (absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the workspace) of a UTF-8 text file.

error.description: Why a directory's own entries are missing (it could not be read).

kind.description: `file`, `dir`, `symlink` or `other`. Symbolic links are listed, never followed.

name_lossy.description:
True when the name on disk is not valid Unicode: `path` shows it with U+FFFD in
place of what could not be decoded, so it cannot be used to reach the entry.

path.description: Path relative to the listed directory, `/`-separated.

lines.description: For a text file of at most 8 MiB: how many lines it has.

link_target.description: Where a symbolic link points, as stored in the link.

made.description: After create_directory: whether this call made it (false: it existed already).

mode.description: Unix permission bits in octal (`0644`); absent on Windows.

path.description: The path, canonical up to its own name (a link is reported as itself).

readonly.description: Whether its permissions mark it read-only.

replaced.description: After move_file: whether a file at the destination was replaced.

size.description: Size in bytes (for a link, the link's own).

path.description: Path (absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the workspace) of a file, directory or symbolic link.

cursor.description: Where to go on from: the previous page's `next_cursor`. Absent for the first page.

depth.description: How many levels below it to include, 0..=3 (default 0: its own entries).

path.description: Path (absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the workspace) of the directory.

entries.description: Directories first at each level, then by name.

next_cursor.description: When it did: pass this as `cursor` for the entries after these, in the same order.

destination.description: Path (absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the workspace) it moves to, on the same filesystem. Its parent directory must exist.

overwrite.description:
Replace a file already at the destination (never a directory). Default false: an
existing destination refuses the move and changes nothing.

source.description:
Path (absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the workspace) of the file, directory or link to move or rename (a link moves as
itself, never what it points to).

line_count.description:
With `start_line`: how many lines, 1..=5000 (default 1000; from a negative
`start_line`, the lines to the end). Never more than `max_bytes` of text.

max_bytes.description: Bytes to read, 1..=24576 (default 24576). Read on from `next_offset` for more.

offset.description:
Byte offset to start at; negative counts back from the end (a tail). Default 0.
With a positive `start_line`: the `next_offset` that came with that `next_line`, so
the line is not searched for again.

path.description: Path (absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the workspace) of the file.

start_line.description:
Read by lines instead of bytes: the 1-based line to start at, or negative to count
back from the end (-50: the last 50 lines). `offset` is then not used.

case_sensitive.description: Match case exactly; by default case is ignored.

context_lines.description: Lines of context before and after each content match, 0..=5.

cursor.description: Where to go on from: the previous page's `next_cursor`. Absent for the first page.

glob.description: Only files whose name matches this glob, such as `*.rs` or `*.{ts,tsx}`.

include_ignored.description:
Also search hidden files and what .gitignore excludes (both are skipped by default,
as git and ripgrep skip them).

path.description: Directory to search (absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the workspace).

pattern.description: What to look for: plain text, or a regular expression with `regex`.

regex.description: Read `pattern` as a regular expression (Rust syntax, like ripgrep's).

bytes_base64.description: The content as base64 bytes. At most 32 KiB of content per call; append for more.

expected_sha256.description:
Overwrite only if the file's current SHA-256 is this (from an earlier write or
edit), so a change made in between is not lost.

mode.description: overwrite (default), create (refuse if it exists) or append.

path.description: Path (absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the workspace) of the file.

text.description: The content as text, written as UTF-8 exactly as given. Give this or `bytes_base64`.

replacements.description: For an edit: how many occurrences were replaced.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of its whole content after the change: pass it as `expected_sha256` next time.

operation_id.description: The operation ID returned by operation_start or run.

HeartbeatOutput.description: Receipt for an explicitly renewed, already admitted hosted process.

expires_at_ms.description:
Acknowledged authority deadline, in Unix milliseconds. Does not extend the
program's own execution deadline or its task lease.

InputMode.description: How an interactive operation takes input.

oneOf.description:
A pseudo-terminal: the program sees a terminal of `cols` by `rows`, echoes what is
typed, and Ctrl-C interrupts it. Output is one stream, `terminal`.
A plain pipe on stdin; stdout and stderr stay separate. Ctrl-C signals the program.

cursor.description:
The output sequence just before this input: what it caused is after it, so read or
wait from here (`operation_read` cursor, `operation_wait` output_after).

InteractiveView.description: An interactive operation's input, as it stands.

input_open.description: Whether `operation_input` can still reach the program.

writer_until_ms.description:
Until when (milliseconds since the Unix epoch) one client holds the keyboard; others
wait or take it over. Absent when nobody holds it.

oneOf.description: What this conversation or client started.

What any conversation of its account started, also before a restart; for this
machine's own account, everything here.

display_command.description: Bounded display preview only. Execute only the exact argv from the canonical request.

interactive.description: How an interactive operation takes input; absent for one that takes none.
Present for an interactive operation: how it takes input and whether it still can.

ownership_scope.description: Root process and its inherited process group only; this is not OS containment.

bytes_base64.description: Raw process bytes, losslessly encoded. Text below is a UTF-8 convenience view.

text.description: Incrementally decoded per stream; split UTF-8 sequences are retained between chunks.

gap.description: True when requested output was evicted from this operation's bounded retention.

broker.description:
This broker, a process it runs under, or another Devagotchi process (its link, an
adapter): stopping it would cut this connection, so kill_process refuses it.

command.description: The command line, cut when very long.

cpu_percent.description: Share of one CPU over a short sample (100 is one whole core).

operation_id.description: The Devagotchi job this process belongs to, when it is one of this broker's.

started_at_ms.description: When it started, ms since the epoch.

user.description: The OS account it runs as.

force.description:
Kill at once (SIGKILL) instead of asking it to stop (SIGTERM). On Windows a process is
always ended at once.

exited.description: Whether it was gone within a few seconds.

filter.description: Only processes whose name or command line contains this (case ignored).

max_results.description: Most processes to return, 1..=1000 (default 200), busiest first.

cursor.description: Last sequence consumed, starting at zero. Reading never advances another reader.

max_bytes.description: Maximum raw bytes to return, 1024..=16384. Frames are at most 1024 bytes.

operation_id.description: The operation ID returned by operation_start or run.
The operation ID returned by operation_start or run.

after.description: Lines just after the match, in order.

before.description: Lines just before the match, in order.

line.description: The matching line's number (1-based), for a content match.

path.description: Path relative to the searched directory, `/`-separated.

text.description: The matching line, without its line ending; a very long line is cut.

complete.description: True when the whole search is done; false with `next_cursor` when there is more.

files_searched.description: Files whose contents this page read (contents searches).

files_skipped.description: Files this page could not search: unreadable, binary, or over 8 MiB.

matches.description:
In path order: a directory's entries by name, each directory's contents where its name
falls. Within a file, by line.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor`, with the same other inputs, for the next page.

stopped_by.description: Why this page stopped early: `max_results` or `time`.

keys.description: Keys pressed after the text, in order (at most 64).

operation_id.description: The operation ID returned by operation_start or run.

take_over.description:
Drive an operation another conversation or client of the same account started, or
take the keyboard from the one holding it. Never reaches another account's.

text.description:
Text to type, exactly as given (UTF-8, at most 16 KiB). Nothing is added: end a line
with the `enter` key.

args.description: Exact argument vector. No shell parsing, interpolation, or added command text.

combined_output.description:
One pipe for stdout and stderr, so the output keeps the order the program wrote it
(as a terminal shows it); every frame is then `stdout`. `run` sets it. Ignored for an
interactive operation, whose terminal already merges them.

command.description:
A command line for the machine's own shell (bash or sh on Linux, Windows PowerShell
on Windows), accepted by a broker that runs commands as its account. Give either
this or `executable` with `args`, not both.

cwd.description:
Working directory (absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the workspace); defaults to the
workspace. A broker that runs only
granted programs keeps it within the workspace.

deadline_ms.description: Execution deadline, not a client wait timeout. 1..=[`MAX_DEADLINE_MS`] milliseconds.

executable.description:
The program to run, with `args`: a name on PATH (`python3`, `cargo`), or a path,
absolute or relative to `cwd`. A script runs with its interpreter (its `#!` line, or
its extension: `.py` with Python, `.ps1` with PowerShell, `.sh` with bash, `.js` with
node), never through a file association; the operation's detail says what ran and why.
On a broker that runs only operator-granted programs the program must be granted.
Leave empty when `command` is given.

idempotency_key.description: A caller-created retry key. The same key and inputs return the same operation.

interactive.description:
Keep the program's input open for `operation_input`: on a pseudo-terminal (`terminal`,
the default: prompts, REPLs, sign-ins, Ctrl-C) or on a plain pipe (`pipe`). Absent:
the program reads nothing (its stdin is the null device), as before.

bytes_base64.description: The raw bytes, base64, when they are not text.

eof.description: Whether this page reached the end of the body.

size.description: The body's length, when the server said it.

text.description: The bytes as text, when they are UTF-8 text.

url.description: The address that answered, after redirects.

offset.description: Where to start in the response body (the previous page's `next_offset`).

operation_id.description: The operation ID returned by operation_start or run.

output_after.description:
Return when output beyond this sequence exists (the cursor you have read up to), as
well as when the operation settles. Without it, return only when it settles.

timeout_ms.description:
Longest to wait, 1..=50000 milliseconds. The answer comes as soon as the operation
changes as asked, without polling; at the limit it comes back unchanged.

oneOf.description:
Replace the file's whole content (atomically: a new file renamed into place), or
create it. The default.
Create the file; refuse when it exists.
Add to the end of the file, creating it when missing.

description:
Export-only schema root. These fields reference canonical Rust DTOs and are
not a broker request or a second set of independently authored contracts.
title: BrokerContracts
